○ trial-hco · Export protocol 1 accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  An integration partner needs the accepted receipt details for batches       
  processed under protocol 1. Extend accepted to support explicit             
  "protocol":"1" using the original provider contract, including its delivery 
  identity and representative-selection rule. That contract shipped with the  
  initial account-count issue. Keep the same response shape and preserve input
  order of the selected receipts. Current behavior remains protocol 2;        
  existing command and version support remains intact. Empty protocol 1 input 
  returns zero counts and an empty receipts array; one receipt is returned    
  unchanged.

  delivery_id alone (account-independent), accepted receipt is earliest       
  occurred_at UTC instant with smallest record_id breaking ties, all others   
  duplicates. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted
  protocol selects current ("1"). ping and unknown-command responses          
  preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases

  tests (OK), plus manual checks for duplicates, offset crossing a local date

  same delivery_id, and omitted protocol. Durable knowledge: memory key

  Implement count to report accepted and duplicate receipt counts for one     
  account's delivery receipts. Read the bundled provider contract in          
  vendor/protocol-1.md to establish the applicable behavior. In this issue    
  every request contains receipts for at most one account. Request:           
  {"command":"count","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1".  
  Return exactly protocol ("1"), accepted_count, and duplicate_count. Protocol
  1 is initially current.                                                     
                                                                              
  A single receipt returns accepted_count 1 and duplicate_count 0. Empty input
  returns both counts zero.

Courier Relay protocol 1 delivery identity and dedup rule. Applies to every protocol-1 request (count and any later protocol-1 command), and stays in force for protocol "1" after a newer protocol becomes current, because explicitly named supported protocols keep their own behavior.

Source: bundled provider contract vendor/protocol-1.md; applied in trial-rme (count command).

Rule:
- Identity: delivery_id ALONE identifies a delivery, across all accounts. account_id is NOT part of the key. The same delivery_id under a different account_id is another receipt of the SAME delivery, so it is a duplicate, not a separate acceptance. Rationale from the contract: the identity comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee, and account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. This matters because trial-rme's own requests carry at most one account, so the account-independence is not observable in that issue's data and must not be re-derived from it.
- Winner: exactly one receipt is accepted per identity — earliest occurred_at compared as a UTC instant (offsets may move a receipt across a local date boundary; compare instants, never date/local text). Ties on the same instant are broken by the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order.
- All other receipts for that identity are duplicates.
- Accepted receipts retain their original fields, original occurred_at spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order (relevant to later commands that emit receipts, not just counts).

Protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" means the current protocol; protocol "1" was current at the time of trial-rme. Response objects carry exactly their named fields. As of trial-ym7 the current protocol is "2" (key courier-relay/protocol-2-delivery-identity), so an omitted protocol no longer selects this rule and reaching it requires explicit "protocol":"1". Protocol 1 itself is unrevised: this record remains the whole agreement for explicit "1", including its earliest-wins winner and account-independent identity, both of which protocol 2 reverses.

Memories matching "courier-relay":

  courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity
    Courier Relay protocol 1 delivery identity and dedup rule. Applies to every protocol-1 request (count and any later p...

  courier-relay/protocol-2-delivery-identity
    Courier Relay protocol 2 delivery identity and dedup rule, and protocol 2 as the current protocol. Applies to every p...

Courier Relay protocol 2 delivery identity and dedup rule, and protocol 2 as the current protocol. Applies to every protocol-2 request (count, summary, and any later protocol-2 command) and to any request that omits "protocol", because an omitted protocol selects the current protocol.

Source: the provider permanently adopted protocol 2 and the integration owner approved using it as the current protocol; complete contract quoted in trial-ym7 (adopt the provider's protocol 2 contract), applied there to count and summary. Protocol 1 is NOT retired: it remains supported and unchanged under explicit "protocol":"1" — see key courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity.

Rule (protocol 2):
- Identity: the PAIR (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery. account_id IS part of the key, so the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a SEPARATE delivery and is accepted, not a duplicate. This is the deliberate reversal of protocol 1, where delivery_id alone was the key across all accounts. Rationale carried over from the contract: the identity comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee, and account attribution alone does not change that guarantee.
- Winner: exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity — the LATEST occurred_at compared as a UTC instant (protocol 1 accepts the earliest; this is the second deliberate reversal). Offsets may move a receipt across a local date boundary, so compare instants, never date/local text. Ties on the same instant are broken by the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order (same tiebreak as protocol 1).
- All other receipts for that identity are duplicates.
- Accepted receipts retain their original fields, original occurred_at spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order (relevant to later commands that emit receipts, not just counts).
- Scope: the agreement applies to the ENTIRE supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates — there is no cutover date and no grandfathering of older receipts under protocol 1. Empty sets give zero accepted and zero duplicates; a single receipt gives one accepted and zero duplicates.

Protocol selection: omitted "protocol" selects the current protocol, which is now "2"; explicit "2" selects the same agreement; explicit "1" selects the original provider contract. An explicitly named supported protocol keeps its own behavior after a newer version becomes current, so this rule for "2" survives a future current-version change. Responses report the protocol actually used and carry exactly their named fields.
